newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico business leaders deny campaign against left.
newsitem.headline: Mexico business leaders deny campaign against left.

text.p: Mexican business leaders on Monday denied accusations they were waging a smear campaign against the country's main leftist party ahead of upcoming mid-term elections.
"There is no campaign to smear anyone, there is no intention to hurt any political party," said Eduardo Bours, head of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), the top private sector business group.
Bours, who on Monday took over the CCE's helm, told reporters business leaders simply wanted to debate and scrutinize economic proposals of the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).

Bours' comments came days after prominent business leaders, including the head of the Mexican Bankers' Association, blasted the PRD's economic platform as populist and warned the economy would suffer capital flight if the party ever gained power.

The criticism was seen by the PRD as a bald-faced attempt by normally pro-government business leaders to discredit the party ahead of July 6 elections, when Mexicans elect most of a new Congress, six state governors and a mayor of Mexico City.
PRD founder Cuauhtemoc Cardenas is well ahead in the polls for the Mexico City race, although the party is seen as having little chance of winning control of Congress.
Banking head Antonio del Valle on Monday backed off from his earlier challenge to the PRD of a debate on economic policy, saying he would rather economists from the private sector debate PRD leaders.
"(My statements) were turned into a political issue, and I do not want it to be that way. That is why I will not debate," he told reporters.
